text: That duration is concerning; have you noticed any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss during this time? Also, do you have a history of smoking or recent exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your smoking history and the duration of the cough, I need to check your lung function and look for any structural abnormalities. REQUEST TEST: Spirometry REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Spirometry: Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) 3.1 L, Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1) 1.9 L, FEV1/FVC Ratio 0.61 (reduced); Chest X-Ray: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no acute infiltrates or obvious masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The spirometry results showing a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio and the X-ray findings of hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms are classic signs of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). Do you experience wheezing or shortness of breath primarily during exertion, and have you noticed any morning headaches or swelling in your ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I definitely get short of breath when I try to play basketball or do any physical work, but I don't wheeze or get morning headaches. My ankles haven't swelled up either, though I do feel quite winded just walking up stairs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your symptoms and test results strongly suggest COPD, have you ever been diagnosed with asthma or experienced similar breathing issues in the past? Additionally, do you currently use any inhalers or other medications to manage your breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: I was diagnosed with COPD five years ago, so I don't have a history of asthma. I do use an inhaler, but I haven't been using it consistently lately because I thought my breathing was okay until recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) exacerbation due to poor inhaler adherence.
